subject: general
question: Diamonds can be synthesised by subjecting pure carbon to:

options.text: very low pressure and high temperature
very high pressure and low temperature
very high pressure and high temperature
very low pressure and low temperature

solution:
The correct answer is **very high pressure and high temperature.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Diamond synthesis** requires the combination of high temperatures and high pressures to convert carbon into its crystalline form.
 
• **High pressure** mimics the natural conditions found deep within the Earth where natural diamonds are formed.
 
• **High temperature** is necessary to facilitate the rearrangement of carbon atoms into the diamond crystal structure.
 
• **Techniques** such as the High Pressure High Temperature (HPHT) method are commonly used in industrial diamond manufacturing.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Concept
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Carbon**
 Carbon is a nonmetallic element, basis of all organic compounds, as well as many inorganic compounds and materials, including diamonds.
 
 

 **Allotropes of Carbon**
 Carbon exists in various forms including graphite, diamond, fullerenes, and graphene, each with unique properties.
 
 

 **Natural vs. Synthetic Diamonds**
 While natural diamonds are formed over billions of years under the Earth's surface, synthetic diamonds are created in laboratories within a few weeks using technological processes.
 
 

 **Applications of Diamonds**
 Beyond jewelry, diamonds are used in cutting, grinding, drilling, and in high-performance electronics due to their extraordinary hardness and thermal conductivity.
